source.title: Representations of Text and Images Align From Layer One
source.authors: Evžen Wybitul; Javier Rando; Florian Tramèr; Stanislav Fort

record.tranche_reason: The study directly investigates text-image representation alignment using a new synthesis-and-transfer method rather than the original studies’ measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own layer-wise synthesis and recognition results, cosine-similarity comparisons, and aggregation ablation. Values used only to select layer-dependent hyperparameters are not recorded as results. Findings cited from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures text-image concept alignment inside one adapter-based VLM, layer by layer, using image synthesis and GPT-5 recognition. It never compares the representations of separately trained models. So it does not test V1–V7, which concern convergence between different models, seeds, or separately trained vision and language models. The paper does not engage the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or convergent learning. The reader's V6 link is wrong: V6 is about how measured cross-model convergence depends on the metric. Here the metric dependence (aggregate vs max-patch cosine) concerns within-model modality alignment, a related but different construct. These findings go under fits_no_version. The closest options are 'discusses' and T6, which are imperfect: the paper neither tests nor cites the claim, but its topic is adjacent.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that VLMs align image and text representations as early as layer 1 for many concepts, without explicit training to do so, and that this follows from end-to-end VLM training. Alignment is uneven across categories, layers and protocols, and results without hints are much weaker. They treat the Gemma middle-layer collapse as likely model-specific, possibly an interaction of their loss with Gemma's middle layers, since InternVL lacks it. They call their results a lower bound, because failed synthesis does not prove absence of alignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cosine-targeted image synthesis and transfer recognition, rather than comparing independently trained models’ representation geometry or scaling model size/performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with layer, category, category hints in the recognition prompt, patch aggregation method, similarity metric, and model. Optimisation also uses layer-dependent hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: In adapter-based VLMs, text-concept vectors have recoverable visual correspondences from layer 1 for some categories. Strength varies by category, layer, model and evaluation protocol. Gemma 3 4B shows a middle-layer collapse that InternVL 3 8B does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within adapter-based VLMs, text and image representations of a concept align from early layers, unevenly across concepts, layers and models.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-model text-image discrimination in Gemma's middle layers depends on the similarity metric. Aggregate cosine loses it, while max-patch cosine keeps a narrowed gap. InternVL shows discrimination under both metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured within-VLM modality alignment depends on how patch representations are aggregated and on the model.

record.problems: The study primarily tests Gemma 3 4B and validates on only one other model and one category there. Recognition is evaluated by GPT-5 rather than human raters; the authors report that results are much weaker without category hints and that many images are not readily human-recognisable. The method is hyperparameter-sensitive, and some successful images contain text rather than pictorial depictions. Several quantitative results are available only in figures; the authors also state that failure to synthesise a recognisable image cannot prove absence of alignment.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models, and no scale or capability sweep.
No alignment between separately trained vision and language models, and no trend with model quality; alignment is measured only inside a single VLM.
No cross-model mapping, stitching, or relative representations.
No comparison of features across models.
Metric dependence is shown only for within-model modality alignment, not for convergence between models.
No measure of convergence between models, and no test of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 links and supports labels are removed: the study's construct is within-model modality alignment, not representational convergence across models. Only two models are used, and InternVL is tested on animals only. Recognition is judged by GPT-5 with GPT-5-mini grading, not by humans.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No comparison of paired image-caption representations across models as both models improve. The study tests text-image concept alignment within VLMs, not alignment growth with model performance.
No comparison across random seeds or shared features/subspaces between same-architecture networks.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test between models.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No out-of-distribution evaluation. The study varies similarity/aggregation choices, image conditions, layer, category, and recognition protocol, but does not test neighbour-count settings.
No test of convergence between independently trained models or whether shared training data/objectives explain it. Layer- and category-dependent alignment within VLMs is not that comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 4B
rows.operation_detail: Compared text-concept cosine similarity with mean-aggregated, centred image-patch representations.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity; matching versus mismatching concept-image pairs
rows.baseline: Mismatching concept-image pairs
rows.value: Matching pairs had higher similarity; p < 0.01
rows.note: The text says matching pairs discriminate reliably in early layers; plotted numeric values are not stated.
rows.check: Within-model text-image cosine discrimination in Gemma 3 4B, not convergence between models; does not bear on V6.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate versus maximum patchwise cosine similarity, especially Gemma 3 4B middle layers
reader_labels.reason: The reported middle-layer discrimination changes with the similarity measure: aggregate similarity shows an anomaly, while maximum patchwise similarity retains a narrowed gap (R2, R4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Recognition protocol, layer, category, aggregation, and model
reader_labels.reason: Recognition varies substantially with category hints, layer, category, aggregation choice, and model; several categories or Gemma middle layers show near-zero results, while other settings succeed (R7–R28).
